policy: One guest vote per network per match; additional voters verify with GitHub without email sign-in

validation.freshDatabaseInstaller: 12 migrations, 34 private application tables, 44 server command names verified
validation.localVoterScreen: GitHub button present, zero email inputs, no horizontal overflow

checks: Two guest browsers holding links for the same network cannot both cast a ballot
Different GitHub identities can vote on shared Wi-Fi; the same identity cannot repeat across browsers or networks
Email accounts, optional X handles and account metadata do not satisfy GitHub verification
A GitHub vote also consumes that network's guest allowance
Network/account changes require a fresh link; used and expired links cannot vote
Vote invalidation and old network-hash cleanup do not restore the active match allowance
Vercel address headers are required in production; arbitrary proxy headers cannot choose the network
IPv6 privacy addresses within one /64 and IPv4-mapped addresses normalize consistently
Failed challenge and ballot attempts consume independent persistent request quotas
GitHub return paths are restricted to internal match URLs and preserve the existing OAuth callback URL
scope: PostgreSQL behavior tested in isolated PGlite fixtures; API/OAuth handlers use mocks. Production checks were read-only after the schema migration. No live test votes, tournaments, payments or accounts were created. Independent hosted connection races were not exercised.
limits: IP networks and GitHub identities do not prove unique people. VPNs, different networks, multiple GitHub accounts, or a person switching between anonymous and authenticated identities can evade some duplication checks. Shared-network voters may need GitHub and are subject to network request quotas.
